name: Publish to Teams
summary: Publishing a BYOM-routed Prompt Agent as a Microsoft Teams app.
description: The Foundry publish-to-Teams flow packages an agent for Microsoft Teams after the agent has been authored in Foundry. The BYOM question is whether an agent whose model is `{connection}/{deployment}` can be published and used in Teams without replacing the orchestrator with a local deployment.
notes:
Verified in the portal: opening the Publish menu on a BYOM-routed Prompt Agent (model = `{connection}/{deployment}`) offers "Teams & Microsoft 365 Copilot" with no BYOM-specific blocking tooltip -- the action is gated by the Foundry account's network configuration (public vs. private), not by whether the orchestrator model is BYOM-routed. This confirms BYOM routing itself is not a blocker for reaching the publish flow.

Not yet verified: whether the published Teams app actually completes a round-trip chat turn end-to-end (only the publish *dialog* was probed, not a live Teams session). Known hard limitation preserved: the SharePoint OBO tool does not work when the agent is published to Teams.

Screenshot evidence exists (`screenshots/01-publish-to-teams-flow.png`) but is withheld from the repo because it shows the real APIM connection name in the Model field -- ask for a re-shoot with the model field cropped/genericized before publishing it on the site.
